etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin integrātus, perfect participle of integrō (“I make whole, I renew, I repair, I begin again”), from integer (“whole, fresh”); see integer, integral.

definitions.definition: To form into one whole; to make entire; to complete; to renew; to restore; to perfect.
To include as a constituent part or functionality.
To indicate the whole of; to give the sum or total of.
(mathematics) To subject to the operation of integration; to find the integral of an equation.
To desegregate, as a school or neighborhood.

quote.citation: 2020 July 18, Bernard Lafayette Jr., “The First Time John Lewis and I Integrated the Buses”, in New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: I continued on the bus without him. It worked out fine. I went on to Tampa, Fla. That was the first time we integrated the buses. All the way down, sitting in the front row.

definitions.definition: (genetics) To combine compatible elements in order to incorporate them.
